note: Tack speaks this line, so "Tack is still in the road" has him name himself in the third person and reads as if someone else is talking about him.
last: Try {#1}. Still 11 Hermits. Tack is still in the road.

note: The after line is unchanged and still says the shop has one of each instead of saying a whorl can hold only one notion.
last: Oh really? The new notions just arrived. // They're small accessories, but they alter how a whorl approaches combat. I've got one of each.

note: The after line starts with a stray "Hermit:" label pasted into the goal text.
last: Hermit: The Hermits moved north toward the machine fields and Hum.

note: The after line is unchanged and still says great-grandmother, which is one generation short of grandmother's grandmother.
last: My great-grandmother wore these boots down from the old shell. They're still solid.

note: The after line still says "I'm twelve" when the old man means his cast is twelve.
last: My cast's ninety, and I'm twelve. Don't ask how. But we both have bad knees, at least.

note: The after line still says unprepared instead of Ouro coming up loose in their shell.
last: I'm taking my place on the Climb. // If you show up unprepared, that's 1 more Hermit added to the roster, and I'm not okay with that.

note: "Keep going" still tells Ouro to move on while Bare blocks the way, when the original only urges Ouro to go ahead and look down.
last: Look back down. Keep going.

note: The after line still says they haul the dust from Rib when they carry water, and "serve her" misreads waiting for the well.
last: Dust remains. We haul it from Rib. The distance is short. I still come to serve her.

note: The notice now says Ouro holds the bowl and no longer says Ouro takes it down, so the line loses that Ouro picks the bowl up.
last: Ouro holds the bowl of upward rain carefully, keeping it upside down.

note: "Mirrors ... but backwards" still stacks two reversals and muddles the hint that the soldier copies Ouro's steps the wrong way round.
last: The soldier mirrors each of Ouro's steps in the opposite pen, but backwards.

note: The after line says the war ended before the speaker was born when the original says before his gran was born.
last: The war ended before I was born. No one told the swords. I won't be the one to break the news.

note: "Worth more to you than a cowrie is to me" garbles the trade, which says the road is worth more than a cowrie to Ouro and less than that to him.
last: Which I'll waive, just this once. // It's worth more to you than a cowrie is to me, so we both come out ahead. I come out aheader.

note: "It came right through your 1 hole" still makes the subject "it" when Tack is the one who came through.
last: It came right through your 1 hole. Thanks for that.

note: The after line is unchanged and still says the measures were measured out instead of saying the cell holds that many measures.
last: {#1} measured out. {sack} remain in the sack.

note: The after line is unchanged and still says the house is empty instead of saying the Sifter now has no house.
last: Just one house. According to my count, it's currently empty.

note: The after line is unchanged and still says the speaker is the only gap in town instead of sitting in it.
last: I dwell between the teeth. I'm the only gap in town, and I got here first.

note: Cinch speaks this line, so "Cinch came down" has him name himself in the third person and reads as if someone else came down.
last: Sit down. Cinch came down when the stamping started. I heard it from the bar.

note: "It's been exactly seventy years since that morning" still frames the day as an anniversary instead of saying this morning was seventy years ago.
last: I'll hear that voice on the bar this morning. It's been exactly seventy years since that morning.

note: The after line drops the negation and now says the Mudlark would not put a door where the Gleaner's feet come, which reverses the clue.
last: Wouldn't put my door anywhere the Gleaner's feet come. Nobody looks where they step.

note: The after line is still a bare x with the surrounding spaces stripped, so the count still runs into the item name.
last: x

note: The after line loses the trailing space after the colon, so the reward name runs into the label.
last: A notion:

note: The after line is still a bare x with the surrounding spaces stripped, so the count still runs into the item name.
last: x

note: "Ease up on the force" and "a lighter touch" still tell you to soften your own effort instead of weakening the whorl before you catch it.
last: Ease up on the force, then catch it. A lighter touch is steadier. // Once you land it, it's yours, and I'm done with that boot.

note: The after line still says the whorl gets away if you fail to knock it out, when the original says a whorl you knock out gets away.
last: (Choose Catch and blow a horn. A successfully caught whorl joins your side. // If you fail to knock it out, it gets away.)

note: The after line starts with a stray "Pump:" label pasted into the question text.
last: Pump: The pump fills every pan to its start and drops every board.

note: The after line starts with a stray "Rider:" label, and "a veteran crane" reads as nonsense.
last: Rider: A veteran crane from the Riders. Equip a GEAR whorl to activate its mechanisms.

note: "It hits what it holds" still makes the foam do the hitting when the original says you hit what the foam holds.
last: Sea foam released by the gray wall. It hits what it holds. The foam keeps the bill. The bill comes. Four cowries, I respect it.

note: "Palm forward" misreads the glove having a face in its palm.
last: A gardener's glove, palm forward. It hurls itself at a companion, who then lands swinging. Five cowries. No pairs.

note: "Bites those who haven't touched it yet" drops that the fog cuts deepest at them, so the bonus damage hint becomes a rule that it only hits untouched targets.
last: At the tide's edge, the fog bites those who haven't touched it yet. Seven cowries. Touch first.

note: "Lasts 0.9 turns" turns the 0.9x damage the dasher takes into a duration, which changes the rule.
last: Dash: lasts 0.9 turns until its next turn. Guard cannot block it.

note: The after line still reads "{#2}'s tide" and treats the amount as an owner.
last: {s.name} runs {#2}'s tide into debt.

note: "{#1} down." still reads as a knockout instead of the whorl being knocked down.
last: {#1} down.

note: "Contains nothing" drops the held-item sense of holds, so it no longer says the whorl holds no notion.
last: {m.name} contains nothing.

note: "It takes 0 5 0 25 damage from projectiles" is garbled and loses the 0.5x general and 0.25x projectile numbers.
last: Acts first in a round. Until your next turn, it takes 0 5 0 25 damage from projectiles, and full damage from dashes. It cannot be forced out.

note: "Reading a waiting foe reveals you are waiting" makes you the one who reads, when the original says a waiting foe's reads see you wait.
last: Wait for the foe to act, then choose. Reading a waiting foe reveals you are waiting.

note: The after line still drops the setting as the target and only says the right side of the board.
last: Setting: Build a machine that carries stones to the right side of the board.

note: The after line is unchanged and still says it returns to the previous match screen instead of rejoining the match the page left.
last: Returns to the previous match screen. The room retains the seat for 90 seconds.

note: "each team holds one species" is garbled, changes the rule to one species per team, and drops that fits count too.
last: {#1} is on {#2} team twice. each team holds one species.

note: "The adjacent cell" loses that the mold copies the stone on its own other cell, which changes the puzzle rule.
last: A mold turns paste into a copy of the stone in the adjacent cell. Note that only one star exists.

note: The after line is unchanged and still reads "{#1} winds turn", which is garbled.
last: {#1} winds turn.

note: "Drops the shield" still reads as the whorl dropping its own shield instead of lifting the shield off its target.
last: {#1} drops the shield.

note: "Many books" misreads texts, which are the move and notion texts in the game.
last: Many books use the % sign. It means parts of 100. 50% is half. 25% is one quarter. 10% is one tenth.

note: "2 moves and 2 habits in total" changes the move rule, since the new whorl keeps 2 moves from each parent.
last: You choose the traits for the new whorl. It keeps 2 moves and 2 habits in total from its parents. It also inherits 1 or 2 types. You also pick its appearance and name.

note: "Tiredness" swaps out fatigue, the name the guide gives this mechanic one page earlier.
last: A round is one turn for each side. Tiredness hits after round {FATIGUE_ROUND}.

note: "Tiredness" swaps out the mechanic name fatigue, and "the slow whorl" drops the comparison to the slower whorl.
last: Tiredness goes past DEF, RES, and Guard. The slow whorl gets hit first.

note: "Tiredness" swaps out fatigue, the name the guide gives this mechanic.
last: No battle can go on forever. Try to win before tiredness starts.

note: "The Inventory" renames the Items pocket of the Bag.
last: The Inventory contains horns and other useful tools, such as a Salt Line.

note: "The nine-oak gate" changes nine spans of oak into nine oaks.
last: No seal, no gate. The Apex sealed the nine-oak gate. No way through, no matter how far you've come.

note: The after line starts with a stray "Tackle:" label pasted into Tack's speech.
last: Tackle: Attempt {#1}. Tackle is ready. Tackle is always ready.

note: "Is still lying" still reads as telling lies instead of things lying about.
last: What the water showed is still lying. I mend it. I put it back together.

note: "Get inside" loses the hint to get in something and can read as going indoors.
last: The Sand Dollar points west. At low water, get inside. Beneath it, scratched: and WIGGLE

note: "Lies flush" still loses that the socket rings flat, and the line drops that it wants the stones it shows.
last: (The socket lies flush, waiting for its stones, each in its proper place.)

note: The after line adds a stray "Fight:" label and changes the short end of the wishbone into a weak spot.
last: Fight: The weak spot.

note: The fix says Knuckle bails when things get tough, which reads as quitting and loses Knuckle's advice to switch whorls.
last: Knuckle always bails when things get tough. I don't. I stick around.

note: The fix drops Rib first, so the line no longer says Rib is the first Sealkeeper to visit.
last: Tell the Sealkeepers. Rib is west along the Midden Road.

note: The fix says the whorl pulled Ouro back in, which loses that it picked Ouro back in return.
last: Look at that. It's pulled you back in. That part's free.

note: The fix still says Leeward has 1 keeper instead of Leeward being the 1 keeper against 11.
last: Leeward's got 1 keeper and there's 11 of them. So I'm gonna help. After I beat you.

note: The fix says the Hermits had better take it slow, so it still loses that the Tusk should come out easily.
last: We're slicing through the Tusk. It's the oldest one around. Better take it slow. Probably.

note: The choice still drops the game term catch and now says Seize it.
last: Seize it

note: The fix says Ouro set the glass room ablaze, which means setting it on fire instead of lighting it.
last: You set the glass room ablaze! I heard it from right here.

note: The fix drops the leading comma that joins this fragment to the text before it, so the joined line runs together.
last: hole filled

note: The fix drops the soup entirely, so Gran's message loses its point.
last: Give my love to my little turnip.

note: The fix changes high water to low water, which reverses the tide the player must swim at.
last: Swim back across the Flats to the Sand Dollar at low water.

note: The fix still says when the next low water arrives instead of how far out the next low goes.
last: The next low water arrives at {#1}{#2}.{walk}

note: The fix still says one to four notches per row instead of one to four notches on each mark.
last: Rows of notched marks, with one to four notches per row, spiral upward around the wall.

note: The fix still turns the reading of the marks into instructions to mark and cut.
last: Mark one, two, three, cutting fresh, then leave a spot for the next.

note: The fix still tells the player to scrape the marks off instead of reading that they were scraped.
last: Newest by the point, oldest first: two notches. Scrape them off. One. Two. Scrape them off.

note: The fix still tells the player to scrape the mark off instead of reading that it was scraped.
last: Four, and a star. Scrape it off. Three. Two. One.

note: The fix still tells the player to scrape three places smooth instead of reading that they are scraped smooth.
last: Then scrape three places smooth.

note: The fix drops at the low, so the next reading's that low has nothing to refer to, and made the last shed reads as a final shed.
last: After the shut one made the last shed, it was soft. It reached in.

note: The fix tells the player to brush a wall to make it ring, which turns the warning into an instruction.
last: (Brush a wall to make it ring. At high tide, three rings and the sea washes you back.)

note: The fix still says it turns over in your palm instead of in the hand.
last: It turns over in your palm. ... Just once.

note: The fix still tells the player to place the nacre in a grotto instead of saying any grotto will layer it on.
last: {r.tan} nacre. place it in any grotto to layer it on.

note: The fix still says when you were my age, and Bezel set the ring at the player's age.
last: Take this ring. I sized it when you were my age, and it has never fit a single finger since.

note: The fix says only the next turn is delayed, and the original says each of the whorl's next turns is delayed.
last: Slow. The whorl's next turn is delayed by 30% of a turn.

note: The fix says only the next turn comes sooner, and the original says each of the whorl's next turns comes sooner.
last: Haste. The whorl's next turn occurs 30% of a turn earlier.

note: The fix says the parts of Rider as if Rider were one person, and Riders are a kind of people.
last: I collect the discarded parts of Rider. Every single one still ticks.

note: The fix changes mind your hat to watch your head, which loses the warning that things float off past the Rim.
last: Beyond the Rim. All is unheld. Watch your head.

note: The choice still drops the game term catch and now says Snag it.
last: Snag it

note: The choice still says Resist it instead of Fight it.
last: Resist it

note: The fix still wraps the horn in the beach glass instead of listing beach glass as a second find, and the trailing lay is garbled.
last: On the sandbar in the inlet, a nautilus horn, rolled up in weed and beach glass, lay.

note: The fix still says do not wake one, and the hint says to wake one.
last: Large ones will sleep on any surface. I'd wager they're resting in my chair. Do not wake one.

note: The fix writes a step in lowercase, which reads the Step stone as an ordinary doorstep and loses the clue.
last: The door faced the water. A step lay in front of the door. // The gate was at the end of the path, toward the water.

note: The fix says Ouro boils the kettle, and the original says Ouro gets the kettle.
last: Ouro boils the kettle.

note: The fix says the old man shed, and the original says his boat shed.
last: I shed last year. Now I've got two boats and no sea.

note: The fix capitalizes eggs, which the original keeps lowercase as a quiet word after the shouting.
last: FORTY YEARS OF HUSHING IN SPIRE. SO TODAY I'M SHOUTING THE SHOPPING LIST. EGGS.

note: The fix replaces the line with the text of the next line about jars of upward rain and loses that rain falls down now.
last: Jars of upward rain. Caught by the trunk. A hundred and twenty a jar. Going up.

note: The fix still says the crane's trunk instead of the trunk.
last: Jars of upward rain. Caught by the crane's trunk. One hundred and twenty per jar. Going up.

note: The fix still says the crater fields slope south instead of saying Fall lies to the south.
last: The crater fields of Fall slope south. Everything here rolls that way.

note: The fix calls it the shell's cast and loses that it is the shell a hole left behind.
last: The shell's cast. It takes stone from what it hits and keeps it. Three cowries. Count your walls afterward.

note: The fix changes a wolf's cast to Tack's cast, which names the wrong subject.
last: Tack's cast, nose down, still on a smell from years back. It sniffs the four cowries before you can hand them over.

note: The fix still pastes the label Ouro into the Register entry.
last: Ouro: A green-inside fallen star, caught in a shell before hitting sand. It closes when hurt. Seven cowries, worth eight.

last: The score is tied at {#1} to {#2}.

note: The fix still starts with it, so the fragment does not follow the whorl name.
last: it is a fit with a plain attack neither parent has.

note: The fix still says this roster holds that many whorls instead of stating the rule that a roster holds them.
last: This roster holds {ROSTER_SIZE} whorls.

note: The fix starts with it, so the fragment does not follow the whorl name.
last: it is a fit with a retune it can't create.

last: This pick holds {TEAM_SIZE} whorls.

last: {#1}'s side is locked for {#2} rounds: its switches go after the other side acts in joint rounds.

last: {#1} stands before {#2}'s bench: it intercepts hits meant for the reserves.

last: Mirage on {#1} shows {o.mirage.hp} having {o.mirage.turns} more HP than it actually does.

note: The fix says the glass breaks, and the original says it turns over as an hourglass does.
last: The glass breaks behind {#1}.

last: {#1} and {#2} trade blows.

last: When a whorl switches out, it sheds most status effects. Burn, Bleed, Poison, Rot, Doom, Ward, Regen, and Hidden remain.

last: Revealed: The whorl shows next turn after Hidden ends. While Revealed, it cannot become Hidden or Untouchable. Hidden: A foe's single hits cannot find it. Its own next hit goes through Guard.

last: Take a seat. They released me at the high tide and brought up soup.

last: Grab it
